description: A plan and policy that makes designing for every road user the routine practice of an agency, rather than something argued for project by project.
scope_notes: This is a standard-practice starting point — edit to your scope. Rename, delete and add records until the list matches the work your agency actually agreed to do.

Every date is calculated forward from the kickoff date you enter. The offsets are round numbers reflecting how this kind of work is usually sequenced — they are placeholders for a real schedule, not commitments.
The hardest part of this work is the last deliverable, not the plan itself: a policy that does not change the project-delivery checklist changes nothing.

No jurisdiction is assumed. Review periods, required notices, hearings and the body that adopts the work are set where you are; none of them are stated here. Add the records your own process requires.
Nobody is assigned. Applying a template never puts a colleague's name on a deadline — assign the records yourself once the team is settled.

deliverables.title: Work plan and stakeholder map
deliverables.summary: The task list, the schedule, and which internal departments must agree for the policy to hold.

deliverables.title: Existing policy, standards and practice audit
deliverables.summary: What the current standards, manuals and habits already require, and where they conflict with the goal.

deliverables.title: Street typology and design toolkit
deliverables.summary: A typology for the network with the design treatments appropriate to each type.

deliverables.title: Network priorities and candidate projects
deliverables.summary: Where the typology changes what gets built first, expressed as a candidate project list.

deliverables.title: Draft complete streets plan and policy
deliverables.summary: The complete draft, including the policy language proposed for adoption.

deliverables.title: Final complete streets plan and policy
Project-delivery checklist
deliverables.summary: The step-by-step check that puts the policy into every project, including the exceptions process and who may approve one.

milestones.title: Project kickoff meeting

milestones.title: Interdepartmental staff workshop
milestones.summary: Public works, planning, maintenance and emergency services work through the trade-offs together.

milestones.title: Public open house
milestones.summary: The typology and priorities shown publicly.

milestones.title: Public review of the draft opens

milestones.title: Adoption of the policy
milestones.summary: Adoption by the body whose adoption makes the policy binding on projects.
